correctness.rationale: The spectral blocks of the weighted sunlet Laplacian yield exact identities for both inverse moments. Strict matrix trace convexity on the mean-zero positive-definite subspace, injective edge-weight parametrization, and averaging under dihedral automorphisms prove unrestricted global uniqueness. The derivative of the exact one-variable F2 objective is the cubic P_n with exactly one positive zero. For every n>=3, the verified positive polynomial T(n-3) proves P_n(t_1)<0, hence t_2>t_1. Leading orders of the cubic give t_2/n -> c, while the first-order square-root allocation gives t_1/sqrt(n) -> 1/sqrt(6); direct expansion yields absolute regret asymptotic to (sqrt(6)/90)n^(11/2). Independently executed check_sunlet.py passed 1009 finite numerical and algebraic diagnostics; those checks are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Primary coherence work establishes the squared-reciprocal Laplacian metric but not sunlet conductance optimization. Effective-resistance design optimizes a different first inverse moment. The weighted corona paper supplies spectral characteristic polynomials and first-order coherence, not the optimized second inverse moment. value.rationale: This is an infinite natural family of two-class unicyclic networks: the precise second-order optimal budget and support are determined against arbitrary asymmetric edge allocation, with a strict all-size structural mismatch from the classical first-order objective. The discrepancy changes the power-law scaling of pendant conductance from n^(-3/2) to n^(-2), and entails a sharp diverging absolute second-order regret. The relative regret tends to zero; no constant-factor penalty is claimed. The result supplies a reproducible spectral-network design benchmark beyond an unmotivated numerical instance.
